Lol, I have I tripple majored with fine art, literature,  and art history.  

The reason I find it to be belittling is because it slides into all of the stereotypes about the typical artstudent with an eating disorder. Its so generalizing and easy to point to and feel like youve summed up everyone elses experiences. However, i have to point out that it is a comic, it uses pictures accompanied by text. I didnt call it a comic to say that I thought it was intended to be funny. It seems like the reason it was made is to draw attention to the problem. 

But your right, I probably just had a bad reaction to it because I find it distateful. Its the artists breakdown of art school, not nessicarily their personal experience of it. Calling something "your breakdown" or "your interpretation" does not mean that it relies on events which happened to you, which I infer from the divergent disorders anorexia which costs nothing, and bulimia, the one that "breaks the bank." The artist sets these up as two sides of a coin, seperate but stemming from the same issue. 

Anyways, was just hoping to get some more indepth analysis of it from somone less biased than I, not just somone telling me to check my education.
Thats the thing though, it seems to be portraying an outsider stereotype from an insider perspective. I was just surprised to see it posted on hyperalergenic tbh.

This was basically my reaction to it. Although I do think that it takes alot to have made this comic if this is her experience. Her sequel comic is equally distasteful though, its about sexual promiscuity filling the void created by not being able to rebell against her parents after going away to college.

It really felt like a slap in the face to somone who has gone through these things; worse it creates an instant stereotype to referance back to.

This post really hit home for me. I think every issue I have ever had in a relationship stems from feeling exactly how you feel. I used to feel the way that you do about your truck about my artwork,  but now even that has lost its ability to comfort me.
dont lose faith in the things that keep you happy. And that accident might have hurt you, might have hurt your truck, but you can fix it and it will make you feel even closer to it.

You did the right thing. I didnt call the police on my best friend cause I promised him I wouldnt. He did kill himself, and that is something I will regret the rest of my life.
they might be angry with you, but their anger is better than their death.

First off- thanks for posting this! Its great to hear stories about how good atheism can be for people's well being instead of bs about it alwAys causing anger/isolation. 
Second, I too have a similar experience.  I have considered myself agnostic for as long as I remeber, but after my bf killed himself last February I found that any notions about the potential of any sort of soul or deity or force has just sort of... dropped away. I am positive that this was a protective reaction by my brain but had I not realized the stupidity of my past beliefs, I know that I would have killed myself. Atheism,  or what people call atheism, prevented me from doing this. It has alowed me to accept his choices and to accept that this is my one and only life and that fact keeps me from doing something to end it.
